samples.summary: Slides toolbar design doc not updated for the new Remove link button; the slides UI decision is filed inside the docs subsystem doc instead
samples.evidence: `slides-toolbar-redesign.md:247-260` is the canonical record of the State-3 text-edit row: it draws the exact button strip `[B] [I] [U] [Aa Color ▾] [🔗 Link]` and states the shared group is "rendered with `showStrikethrough={false}` and `showHighlight={false}`", and line 260 repeats the same prop list for the mobile `TextFormatSheet`. This change adds a third prop (`showRemoveLink`) and a new visible button to both of those exact call sites (`text-edit-section.tsx:93`, `mobile-toolbar.tsx:580`) but leaves the doc's row diagram and prop list stale. The rationale is instead written into `docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md` §"Removing a link on slides" — a docs-area doc describing slides toolbar composition, i.e. the decision now lives away from the subsystem doc that owns it. Nested design docs are not link/ref-checked by CI, so nothing else catches the drift.

samples.summary: `removeLink` now means two different things on two surfaces: selection-first in the text box, caret-only in docs
samples.evidence: The text-box `removeLink` gains "a selection wins over the caret" (`text-box-editor.ts:1239-1258`), while the docs `EditorAPI.removeLink` (`packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3737-3755`) still resolves purely from `cursor.position` via `findLinkRunAt`. The shared frontend contract added in `text-formatting/types.ts:94-107` even codifies the split ("A selection takes precedence over the caret *where the implementation supports one*"), so one named command has two documented behaviours. Docs happens to reach it only from a caret-opened popover today, but the divergence is exactly the kind that drifts further (cf. the hand-rolled `clearFormatting` key list this same change had to re-converge). Cost stays inside the codebase for now, hence minor.

samples.summary: `pendingStyleFor` changes collapsed-caret behaviour for every toolbar style write (Bold, colours, font-size stepper), which is beyond the issue's outcome and plan
samples.evidence: The task file `docs/tasks/active/20260908-docs-clear-formatting-keeps-links-todo.md` scopes the change to five items about `CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE`, the Cmd+\ shortcut, contract comments, the design doc and tests; its acceptance criteria are all about Clear formatting and `removeLink`. `pendingStyleFor` instead injects `href: undefined` into the seed of *every* collapsed-caret style write, so Bold / colour / font-size at a link's trailing edge now stop extending the link — a pre-existing behaviour (the seed already carried `href` before this change) altered for commands the issue never mentions. It is defensible as regression-prevention for the sibling buttons, but it is unrequested behaviour change riding along with the fix and should at least be called out as such.

samples.summary: The 're-arm the link exit' rule is hand-copied into two editors instead of being shared next to `isAtLinkTrailingEdge`
samples.evidence: `TextEditor.clearFormatting` (`text-editor.ts:3440-3448`) and `EditorAPI.pendingStyleFor` (`editor.ts:1189-1198`) each recompute the identical predicate `isAtLinkTrailingEdge(...) || !!(prev && 'href' in prev && prev.href === undefined)` and each hand-compose the `{ ...style, href: undefined }` result. The change went to the trouble of extracting the caret walk into one shared `model/caret-style.ts` export precisely because a copied caret walk drifted before (#715 is cited in the design doc), yet the rule built on top of it is duplicated in the same commit. Two copies, two chances to diverge on what "exits a link" means.

samples.summary: New user-facing Slides/mobile Remove-link control is scope beyond the issue, added in the same change as the model fix
samples.evidence: The issue's plan and acceptance list (`docs/tasks/active/20260908-docs-clear-formatting-keeps-links-todo.md:20-49`) say nothing about a new toolbar button; item 5 asks only for tests. This change adds a `showRemoveLink` prop, a new button, opt-ins on desktop (`text-edit-section.tsx:93`) and mobile (`mobile-toolbar.tsx:580`), a new selection code path in `TextBoxEditorAPI.removeLink`, and a new frontend test file. The motivation given (Slides has no link popover, so preserving `href` through Clear formatting would leave no removal path) is sound and arguably a consequence of the outcome — but it is a separate user-facing feature bundled into a model-semantics fix, and it changes a shared component used by the docs toolbar too.

samples.summary: Acceptance criterion 'same behaviour in the slides text-box editor' holds only for range clears; the collapsed-caret clear behaves differently there
samples.evidence: The new text-box test's own comment states the slides entry point "stages nothing at a collapsed caret", so after Clear formatting at a link's trailing edge a typed ordinary character still inherits the link on slides, while docs (via `pendingStyleFor`) exits it. The issue asks for "Same behaviour in the slides text-box editor"; the range case matches, the collapsed-caret case knowingly does not. Documented as intentional in `docs-font-controls.md:318-325`, so this is a recorded divergence rather than an omission — but it is a divergence against a stated criterion.
